weeks.context: Mobile is HARD because phones are HARD — limited memory, flaky network, weird screen sizes, app stores that gate-keep. Week 1 you learn React Native + Expo and ship a real app to YOUR OWN phone by Sunday. No emulator-only nonsense.

days.title: Why React Native + Expo
days.summary: Build once, run on iOS and Android. Save your sanity.

items.title: Expo vs bare React Native — which to use 2025
items.creator: various

items.title: What will you build?
items.body: Pick ONE useful tool for YOUR life: a habit tracker, a workout timer, a daily journal, a price-watch list, a class schedule. Must be something YOU would open every day.

days.title: Set up Expo + run on your phone
days.summary: If it doesn't run on your phone today, the rest of the week is wasted.

items.title: Hello phone
items.body: Install Node.js + Expo Go on your phone. Run `npx create-expo-app forge-mobile-week1`. Run `npx expo start`. Scan the QR with Expo Go. See 'Open up App.js to start working on your app!' on your phone screen.

days.title: React + JSX fundamentals
days.summary: If you've never seen React, this is the day.

items.title: Components
items.body: Make a `Header.js` component that takes a `title` prop and renders it. Import it in App.js. Pass 3 different titles.

days.title: useState — the only hook you need this week
days.summary: State is the heartbeat of any app.

items.title: Counter or toggle
items.body: Build a button that, when tapped, increments a number on screen. Then add a 'Reset' button. Then style the buttons with `TouchableOpacity` + StyleSheet.

days.title: Lists, navigation, persistence
days.summary: Real apps have screens and remember things.

items.title: AsyncStorage in Expo — save data on device
items.creator: various

items.title: List + storage
items.body: Build a list screen with `FlatList`. Render 3 hard-coded items. Add a button that adds a new item to the list. Save the list to AsyncStorage so it survives app restart.

days.title: Style it like a real app
days.summary: Buttons should feel like buttons. Animations matter.

items.title: Polish
items.body: Make your app look intentional: a real color palette, real font sizes, padding that feels right on a phone. Use `SafeAreaView`. Test on both phone orientations.

days.title: Ship — APK / TestFlight
days.summary: It's not done until it's installed on a phone other than yours.

items.title: Build the passport app
items.body: Polish your app into one finished thing. Push to GitHub. Run `eas build` for Android (free) and get an APK link. Send it to a friend over WhatsApp. Have them install it and use it for a day. Get their feedback.

items.title: What did they actually do?
items.body: Did your friend open the app? Use it once? Use it twice? Never open it? What does that tell you about the value of what you built?

topics: JavaScript ES2020+ refresher (arrow fn, async, destructuring)
React components, props, state
JSX, TouchableOpacity, FlatList, SafeAreaView
useState (rest of hooks later)
React Navigation — Stack
AsyncStorage for local persistence
Expo Go workflow + EAS build basics
tasks: Install Node.js + Expo CLI + Expo Go on your phone
Initialize a new Expo app and run it on your actual phone
Build a 2-screen app with navigation
Persist data with AsyncStorage so it survives restart
Style with flexbox + StyleSheet to look real
Build an APK with EAS and install it on a friend's phone
Get one real user's feedback by Sunday
weeks.project: Pick something YOU would use every day — a habit tracker, water reminder, expense logger, anything. Build it in Expo, install it on your phone, install it on one friend's phone. Get their reaction. The 'app store' part doesn't matter yet — a real APK on a real phone IS a portfolio piece.
exercises: Add a delete-item button to your list with a confirmation dialog
Add light/dark mode using `useColorScheme()`
Use the device's haptic feedback on button press (`expo-haptics`)

questions: What would make your friend actually open the app tomorrow without you nagging?
What breaks if they have no internet? Should it work offline?
What's the smallest version of this app a stranger would pay $1/mo for?
If iOS people use your app, what looks wrong vs Android?

weeks.title: React Native and Expo — The Productive Path
weeks.context: Expo turns React Native from a frustrating native build chain into a one-command development loop. Most cross-platform mobile shipping in 2025 happens on Expo. This week you build fluency with the core components, layout, and the EAS build/submit pipeline.
topics: Expo Router — file-based routing, layouts, deep links
Core components — View, Text, ScrollView, FlatList, Image, Pressable
Layout — Flexbox in React Native (defaults differ from web)
Styling — StyleSheet, inline styles, the case for nativewind (Tailwind for RN)
TouchableOpacity vs Pressable — why Pressable wins
FlatList performance — keyExtractor, getItemLayout, why ScrollView fails at scale
Expo modules — Camera, Location, Notifications, FileSystem, ImagePicker
EAS Build + Submit — building production binaries and submitting to stores
tasks: Start a new Expo project with `npx create-expo-app -t default-typescript`; explore the file-based routing
Build a tab navigation with 3 tabs: Home, Search, Profile
Build a FlatList of 1000 items; verify smooth scrolling on a real device
Install nativewind and configure Tailwind classes; verify they compile
Use EAS Build to produce an iOS development build; install it on your phone
weeks.project: Build a Recipes App scaffold. 3 tabs: Recipes (list view), Favourites (filtered list), Profile (your settings). Use Expo Router for navigation. FlatList for the recipes (use a public API like TheMealDB). Pull-to-refresh, infinite scroll, swipe-to-favourite. Test on real iOS and Android devices. This becomes the base you'll extend in weeks 3-8.

Deep links — universal links on iOS, app links on Android
Tab bar customisation — icons, badges, hide-on-scroll
Navigation state persistence — restoring on app relaunch
Type-safe navigation — Expo Router's typed routes
tasks: Add a stack navigator with at least 3 levels deep; verify back gestures work on iOS
Add a modal that slides up from the bottom; dismiss with swipe-down gesture
Configure deep links: opening your-app://recipe/123 navigates to the recipe page
Add a custom header with a search field and a right action button
Add a badge to a tab bar icon (e.g. notification count)
weeks.project: Extend Recipes App with Full Navigation. Add: a detail screen for each recipe (push), a half-sheet modal for filters, a settings screen accessible from Profile tab (push), a 'Recipe of the Day' modal that appears on first launch. Configure deep links so a recipe URL opens directly to its detail. Test all of this on both platforms — gestures, transitions, animations.

weeks.title: Lists, Performance, and the FlatList Mindset
weeks.context: 90% of mobile UI is lists. Slow lists ruin apps. This week you master FlatList, SectionList, FlashList — the libraries and patterns that keep scrolling at 60fps even with thousands of items.
topics: Virtualised lists — only rendering what's visible
FlatList vs FlashList (Shopify) — when each wins
keyExtractor — why this matters for performance
getItemLayout — skipping layout calculations for fixed-height rows
windowSize and maxToRenderPerBatch — tuning for memory vs smoothness
Pull-to-refresh + infinite scroll patterns
Empty states, error states, loading skeletons in lists
Profiling — Flipper, React DevTools profiler, Hermes Debugger
tasks: Replace your FlatList with FlashList (from Shopify); measure scrolling smoothness on a low-end device
Add getItemLayout to a fixed-height row list; verify scroll-to-index becomes instant
Add a SectionList grouped by date or category
Profile a janky list with React DevTools profiler; identify the wasted re-renders
Add skeleton loading + empty state + error state to a real list screen
weeks.project: Build a Feed Screen with 10000+ items. Use FlashList. Each item is a card with an image, title, and metadata. Pull-to-refresh at the top, infinite scroll at the bottom. Profile on a real low-end Android. Ship 60fps scrolling. Document the optimisations you made.

weeks.title: Forms, Inputs, and Keyboard Handling
weeks.context: Mobile keyboards are the most painful UI element. This week you learn keyboard avoidance, input validation, secure text entry, and form patterns that don't make users want to throw their phones.

Focus management — focus next field on submit, dismiss keyboard on outside tap
Multi-step forms — wizard pattern, progress indicators
Native input alternatives — date pickers, time pickers, pickers

weeks.project: Build a Multi-Step Onboarding Flow. 4 screens: welcome, account details (email, password), profile (name, photo via camera), preferences (toggles). Progress indicator at top. Each step validates before advancing. Persists progress so user can leave and resume. Test on both platforms — especially the keyboard handling on iOS notch devices.

Performance — keep work on the UI thread; never run gesture math on JS
Lottie — pre-made animations from After Effects

weeks.title: Local Storage — AsyncStorage, MMKV, SQLite

Storage limits — what each platform actually allows
Backup considerations — iCloud, Google Drive backup, what to opt out of

weeks.title: Updates, Versioning, and OTA
weeks.context: App Store reviews take days. Sometimes you need to ship a fix right now. EAS Update + Expo Updates let you push JS-only changes over-the-air, instantly. This week you wire it up — and learn what's safe to push that way.
topics: EAS Update — pushing JS bundles without going through the store
Versioning strategy — semantic version, build number, JS bundle version
What's safe to OTA — JS changes only; never native
Channels and branches — staging vs production updates
Rollback — how to revert a bad OTA in minutes
Force update prompts — for breaking native changes
App Store review rules around hot updates
Update download UX — silent vs prompted
tasks: Enable EAS Update in your project; configure channels: staging and production
Push a JS-only update to staging; verify it lands on testers' devices
Promote a tested update from staging to production
Implement a 'check for updates' UI that prompts users to restart on critical fixes
Practice a rollback: ship a bad update, roll back, verify users get the previous version
weeks.project: Set Up OTA Updates for Recipes App. Staging channel for testers, production channel for everyone. Implement a 'force update' modal for changes that require a native rebuild. Document the update strategy: what's safe to OTA, what needs a store release. Push 3 updates across a week to verify the loop.

weeks.title: App Store Optimisation — Getting Found and Installed
weeks.context: A great app no one downloads is no app at all. App Store Optimisation (ASO) — keywords, screenshots, ratings, conversion rate — is the difference between obscurity and growth. This week you treat your store listing as a product.
topics: Keyword research — App Store + Play Store search algorithms
Title, subtitle, keyword field — the prioritisation
Screenshots — the first three are everything
App preview video — when it converts, when it doesn't
Ratings and reviews — soliciting, responding to, lifting average
Localised store listings — different by country
Featured opportunities — what Apple and Google look for
ASO tools — Sensor Tower, AppFollow, App Annie (data.ai)
tasks: Pick 5 candidate keywords for your app; check competition with AppFollow's free tier
Rewrite your app title, subtitle, keyword field around your top 5 keywords
Redesign your first 3 screenshots — feature the value, not the UI
Implement in-app rating prompt at a positive moment (after a successful recipe save)
Write a localised store listing in Spanish
weeks.project: Optimise Your Recipes App's Store Listings. Research keywords with intent, restructure title/subtitle/keywords, redesign first 3 screenshots with text overlays selling the value, write a value-led description, set up in-app rating prompts. Get 5 real ratings. Document the ASO decisions in ASO.md.

weeks.title: Capstone — Ship to Both Stores, Real Users
weeks.context: The final week. You take everything from weeks 1-23 and you push a real app to the App Store and Play Store with real users. By Sunday it's live, downloadable by anyone, in TestFlight or external testing. This is the artifact.
topics: Scoping for store submission — what passes review on first try
Final asset polish — icon, screenshots, video
Privacy nutrition labels — what data you collect, what you share
Required legal — privacy policy, terms of use, COPPA if relevant
Pre-launch checklist — every box, ticked
Submission strategy — first-time review takes 1-3 days, plan for re-submission
Launch day — how to push the first install spike
First week of feedback — triage, respond, iterate
tasks: Pick ONE app to ship. Either Recipes or something new.
Write a public-launch checklist before any code
Talk to 5 potential users before final code; record what they said
Hard deadline: app live in the App Store AND Play Store (or in external test track) by Sunday
Plan the launch — what channels, what message
weeks.project: Ship one app, real distribution. Either Recipes (your roadmap project) or something else you actually want to use. Must include: real users, real reviews, real install funnel data, full observability, real metadata, real privacy policy, accessibility tested, internationalised. Launch publicly — Twitter, your audience, ProductHunt mobile category, r/sideproject. Get at least 50 installs in the first week. Document the entire journey in LAUNCH.md.
